title: Retries Are a Distributed Systems Bug Waiting to Happen: Runtime Invariants and Algorithmic Bounds in Go
topic: Retries Are a Distributed Systems Bug Waiting to Happen: Designing Idempotent APIs
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: Retries in distributed services often expose hidden race conditions and state inconsistencies. We present a Go-based engine that enforces idempotent request handling by coupling a synchronized idempotency map with a lightweight resource store. The engine guarantees that each unique idempotency key maps deterministically to a single response, thereby eliminating duplicate side effects even under concurrent retries. We formalize the causal ordering invariant that the engine preserves a strict height-balanced key-ordered structure for the idempotency map, ensuring $O(\log n)$ lookup and insertion. Empirical evaluation on an AMD EPYC 7763 host yields a mean latency of 1399.27 \textmu{}s, a P95 latency of 2287.16 \textmu{}s, and a throughput of 714,659 ops/s over 30 iterations. The source code is publicly available at \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/go-concurrency-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261024_110150_retries_are_a_distributed_syst}.
